clue:plaque.text: Small brass plate under the candles: NORA GRACE CALLOWAY, 1989–2009. “Lord, to whom shall we go?” Somebody’s daughter.
clue:plaque.title: A plaque at the shrine

clue:postcard.text: She read the back of my postcard twice. Asked who A.H. was like she didn’t care. She cared.
clue:postcard.title: The postcard

note:alarm.text: Everybody on the lawn in what they sleep in. Theo saved the espresso machine. Margot wrote ‘ALARM 1’ like it was a case number.
note:alarm.title: Fire alarm, 3:07 a.m.

note:assignment.text: Two pages a week, bled on in red. Her next one: a broken statue is still Herakles. I’m going to need more pens.
note:assignment.title: Designated antagonists

note:cigarette.text: An Altoids tin from a pea-soup restaurant in Buellton. RELIQUARY on the lid. No. 1: the Lighthouse, 8/29. She’s keeping count.
note:cigarette.title: The Reliquary

note:driveway.text: The guy at the end of the driveway is my TA.
note:driveway.title: The guy at the end of the driveway

note:fence.text: A gap in the fence behind the Lighthouse; a path along the bluff to the Point. Two people today told me not to go there. Neither would say why.
note:fence.title: The path

note:la_flaca.text: Rafi’s bike, lent till Christmas. Not stolen. Abandoned. (A week’s difference, per his abuela.)
note:la_flaca.title: La Flaca

note:ledger.text: Pie: paid. Bus fare: paid, with compliments. Richard Vance’s hundred: Theo’s, for the gas. It’s been through the pool.
note:ledger.title: The ledger

note:malibu.text: The bottom half of the pie Post-it, still on the espresso machine in Theo’s hand. Theo says it’s open. I believe him.
note:malibu.title: + 1 Malibu

note:newman.text: The roof is an upside-down boat. The lector reads Deuteronomy like he’s running for Congress. The cantor could make a rock cry.
note:newman.title: St. Brendan’s

note:pelican.text: A girl across the quad won an argument with a parking cop while holding a lamp shaped like a pelican. I didn’t catch her name. I didn’t catch anything. Dad says close your mouth.
note:pelican.title: Pelican girl

note:pie.text: Marionberry: 4/10 (now on a board by the register). I work here now. Tue/Thu/Sat, seven to one, $8 an hour.
note:pie.title: The Anchor

note:pie_paid.text: Paid Theo one peach pie, Lena’s mother’s crust. Marionberry still 4/10.
note:pie_paid.title: Pie

note:seminar.text: Hale’s seminar. Monday, 1 p.m., Hollis 302. One of the twelve is M. Broussard.
note:seminar.title: PHIL 9H

note:soprano.text: Parish hall, bulletins, lemon bars. “We lost our best soprano last spring.”
note:soprano.title: Mrs. Fitch

note:the_point.text: A cliff, according to Priya. “Next.” Nobody goes there after dark. Her rule, not the school’s.
note:the_point.title: The Point

note:theo_dawn.text: Came in barefoot at 5:20, sand and wet jeans. “Couldn’t sleep.” There was a girl in our room.
note:theo_dawn.title: Theo, 5:20 a.m.

person:becca.text: Coeur d’Alene. Seven siblings. Can butcher a deer. Running the Sept 19 BBQ like a cattle drive. Asked if I had a girlfriend. For the seating chart.
person:becca.title: Becca (Newman)

person:caleb.text: Visalia. Has Hale’s book so full of Post-its it’s molting. Says ‘Selah’ when he means ‘touché.’
person:caleb.title: Caleb (PHIL 9H)

person:danny.text: My brother. Trumbull Correctional. Calls me Professor. Ma brought him the good socks.
person:danny.title: Danny

person:evan.text: Thursday section, Hollis 108. Kierkegaard. Kind to the scared ones, murder on the lazy ones. Smokes American Spirits. Rides a bike.
person:evan.title: Evan Marsh (TA)

person:frank.text: Frank Costigan. Twenty-six years on the line at Lordstown, laid off since June. Drove me 2,400 miles because two plane tickets cost more than the truck is worth. Saw the Pacific for the first time today. Didn’t say anything. That’s how you know.
person:frank.title: Dad

person:gloria.text: Hired me for rating her pie a four. Rated me a lattice-top. I’m not going to ask.
person:gloria.title: Gloria (the Anchor)

person:hale.text: Wrote *The Consolations of Disbelief*. Wrote me a postcard. Walked into Hollis 302 at 1:07 with wine on his cuff and asked us to prove we have souls. Knew my face from the Anchor before he knew my name. Called me a spaniel.
person:hale.title: Prof. Adrian Hale

person:kevin.text: Kevin Tran. Goes to daily Mass, saves you a seat with a Bible. Has a sister, Tina, in dental school, who flossed in the womb. Lies to his mom about orgo in Vietnamese. Drives his mother’s Odyssey at sixty-five, not sixty-six. His dad has two nail-salon supply stores in San Jose and has never had a Labor Day.
person:kevin.title: Kevin Tran

person:laney.text: Laney Price. Practicing for Pi Lam like it’s the Olympics. Programmed herself into my phone. First Catholic Mass: arms crossed like a Baptist, came back from the blessing pink and quiet. (Hoodie status: hers.)
person:laney.title: Laney Price

person:lena.text: New Orleans. Two seventeen. Classics. Hale paired us for the semester. Makes a roux like she’s taking a vow and expects you to keep up. Her father sells Gulf shrimp — Broussard’s Seafood, Banks Street. Boyfriend: Wes Arceneaux — Tulane, civil engineering, the boat at sixteen. Called at 8:04 on the dot.
person:lena.title: Lena Broussard

person:margot.text: Margot Lindqvist. Has a folder on me. Called Lena and me useful idiots for Christian nationalism in front of four hundred people. Made a point about the Euthyphro I still can’t answer. Her mother teaches Classics at Reed. Doesn’t sleep. Possibly my friend.
person:margot.title: Margot Lindqvist

person:osei.text: Newman chaplain. Kumasi, Ghana. Used to be a doctor. Limps and doesn’t mention it. Plays chess like he’s got all night and highlife like the neighbors owe him money. Told me a proverb about funerals. I laughed. That was apparently the point.
person:osei.title: Fr. Gabriel Osei

person:poppy.text: Theo’s sister. Fourteen. He always picks up.
person:poppy.title: Poppy

person:priya.text: Laminates things. Owns an air horn. Has one rule she doesn’t laminate.
person:priya.title: Priya (RA)

person:rafi.text: Second floor. Carried my fridge up four flights on Saturday and was gone before Dad could tip him. Calls everybody boss. Lent me his bike on the wharf at one in the morning like it was nothing.
person:rafi.title: Rafi (204)

person:richard.text: Theo’s father. Learned everybody’s name in one pass but mine; thought I came with the caterer. Calls him Teddy. Stayed six minutes, fourteen seconds. Margot timed it.
person:richard.title: Richard Vance

person:rudy.text: Line cook. Rosary on his wrist, a ballgame on the radio, Louis L’Amour in his apron. Did six years at Soledad. Says the dish pit is the best job in any building.
person:rudy.title: Rudy (the Anchor)

person:theo.text: Roommate. Drives his grandfather’s car like a getaway. His father calls him Teddy and stays six minutes. Heard my brother’s voice and didn’t ask.
person:theo.title: Theo Vance

person:yusuf.text: Fremont. Engineer. Fasting for Ramadan through a ninety-minute seminar and funnier than all of us.
person:yusuf.title: Yusuf (PHIL 9H)

keys.text: You shook your father’s hand goodbye.
Lena took the cigarette out of your mouth.
You walked Lena and Laney home.
You gave Fr. Osei a straight answer about the scar, and he didn’t push.
At Mass you prayed for the girl three pews up.
You followed Lena out of the Anchor.
You let Lena know you were on the stairs.
You hit Reply All.
You told Hale he’d inherited his atheism too.
You took Theo’s money as a loan, payable in pie.
You told your father you’d taken a job washing dishes.
You played chess with Fr. Osei instead of going to confession.
You told Lena you’d been worried she had bad taste.
You wrote on Lena’s wall at two in the morning.
You walked Laney to Pi Lam with Lena.
You told Theo you couldn’t afford Los Angeles.
You told Theo God is the one who pays.
You told Margot a nun gave you the scar.
You told Nonna you played chess with the priest instead of going to confession.
You spent Sunday afternoon at the Getty Villa with Lena.
You gave Richard Vance’s hundred to Theo for the gas.
You told Lena your father’s been laid off since June.
You told Theo where your brother is.
You gave Lena’s reliquary its second relic.

S1E01.choice: “Thanks for driving me, Dad. All of it.”
“I’m going to marry that girl.”
Hang it a little lower, so it’s “not watching your side.” Then the eyebrow: a swan.
Handshake. Steady. Man to man.
S1E01.key: You shook your father’s hand goodbye.

S1E01.choice: “I’m going to be a priest. I’m going to be a philosopher. I’m going to be extremely good at beer pong.”
Light a Marlboro Red instead.
The living room, where a redhead is dancing on a coffee table.
“I’m not sad. I’m Irish. It’s a different thing.”
“Knife-juggling at the St. Anthony’s pierogi festival. The Ukrainians did it.”
“That’s classified.”
Light a Marlboro. Offer her one.
S1E01.key: Lena took the cigarette out of your mouth.

S1E01.choice: Take Laney’s other arm. Walk them home.
S1E01.key: You walked Lena and Laney home.

S1E01.choice: “Tell her to drink water. And — goodnight, Lena.”
“He doesn’t hate anybody. That’s the problem — He loves everybody and expects things from them.”
“A fight. A long time ago. Long story.”
S1E01.key: You gave Fr. Osei a straight answer about the scar, and he didn’t push.

S1E01.choice: Pray for the girl three pews up — and then for yourself, since you’ve clearly lost your mind.
S1E01.key: At Mass you prayed for the girl three pews up.

S1E01.choice: Augustine: *Dilige, et quod vis fac.* Love, and do what you will. Get the love right and the forms follow.
Kierkegaard: a whole nation baptized and nobody a Christian. “When the form is all you’ve got, you end up with Denmark. Or Boston yesterday.”
Spring it first. “You just argued the heart over the form. Welcome to my side of the courtyard.”
Give her the last word anyway.
Follow her out.
S1E01.key: You followed Lena out of the Anchor.

S1E01.choice: Tell her a brand-new, ridiculous scar story to make her laugh.
Tell Mom about the girl. A little.
Cough. Let her know you’re there.
S1E01.key: You let Lena know you were on the stairs.

S1E01.choice: Let Theo dare you into Reply All: “Looking forward to it. —Jack (Youngstown).”

S1E02.choice: Pull off the Mooney hoodie and hold it out to her.
Side with her and push further: the intellect holds *triangle* and *justice*, which no organ can. Aquinas, *ST* I q.75 a.2.
Smash the piano and you haven’t disproved the pianist. Aquinas got there first: injure the organ and understanding is *impeded*.
“We’re both right, and he’s counting on us not to notice.” Turn on Hale together.
Newman: how a belief got into you says nothing about whether it’s true. And Hale got his from somebody too.
S1E02.key: You told Hale he’d inherited his atheism too.

S1E02.choice: “Bleed on mine. I can take it.”
“A loan. With interest. I’ll pay you in pie.”
S1E02.key: You took Theo’s money as a loan, payable in pie.

S1E02.choice: “They’d be lucky.”
Side with Lena: “The Church made a dyer’s daughter from Siena a Doctor of the Church. She told a pope to go back to Rome, and he went. Try again.”
“I’ve seen your marionberry. You need me.”
“So I’m in good company.”
Tell him about the job.
S1E02.key: You told your father you’d taken a job washing dishes.

S1E02.choice: “Put me down.”
“The board.”
S1E02.key: You played chess with Fr. Osei instead of going to confession.

S1E02.choice: One more joke. “Is that a real proverb, or did you make it up just now?”
Match his dad jokes: “Why did the pre-med cross the road?”
Bum a cigarette: “American Spirit. You *are* a grad student.”
“Good. I was starting to worry you had bad taste.”
S1E02.key: You told Lena you’d been worried she had bad taste.

S1E02.choice: Hold out the whole pack: “Save us both the trouble.”
Write on her wall: “Bus fare: $1.25. Interest accrues. —Youngstown”
S1E02.key: You wrote on Lena’s wall at two in the morning.

S1E02.choice: Walk Laney to the open house.
S1E02.key: You walked Laney to Pi Lam with Lena.

S1E02.choice: “How long have you known her?”
Take it, and hand it to Lena without drinking.
“I can’t afford LA, Theo.”
S1E02.key: You told Theo you couldn’t afford Los Angeles.

S1E03.choice: “Put it under the pie.”
Ride with Theo in the SL.
“Tell me about Poppy.”
“First-, second-, third-class relics. What class is a Marlboro?”
Cannonball contest with Laney.
Turn the Meters up and make the stirring a show for Laney’s BlackBerry.
“He’s the one who pays. That’s the whole scandal.”
S1E03.key: You told Theo God is the one who pays.

S1E03.choice: “Sister Mary Clement. Third grade. A ruler. She was aiming for my soul.”
S1E03.key: You told Margot a nun gave you the scar.

S1E03.choice: “No, Nonna. I played chess with the priest.”
S1E03.key: You told Nonna you played chess with the priest instead of going to confession.

S1E03.choice: The Getty Villa with Lena and Margot.
S1E03.key: You spent Sunday afternoon at the Getty Villa with Lena.

S1E03.choice: “A statue doesn’t feel the arm go.”
Hand it straight to Theo: “For the gas.”
S1E03.key: You gave Richard Vance’s hundred to Theo for the gas.

S1E03.choice: Benedict wants gift *inside* the economy — gratuitousness. *Caritas in Veritate*, thirty-six. A tip is the gift.
Subsidiarity. *Quadragesimo Anno*, seventy-nine: don’t hand to the big what the small can do. The national union is the big.
“The bailout saved GM, not the men. The CEOs flew in on jets. My father got a letter. Twenty-six years at Lordstown.”
S1E03.key: You told Lena your father’s been laid off since June.

S1E03.choice: “Twenty-six years of cars. Sunday gravy. A garage you could eat off of.”
Describe the ocean, plainly.
Tell it plain: “He’s in Trumbull. Five years. A fight — a guy got hurt bad. Three more to go, maybe less.”
S1E03.key: You told Theo where your brother is.

S1E03.choice: Light it anyway.
S1E03.key: You gave Lena’s reliquary its second relic.

S1E03.choice: “Family stuff. It’s good, actually. Mostly.”
Text Gina: tell him happy Labor Day.
